lyrics:
[Intro: bouncing synth bass, drum machine, record scratch]

[Verse 1: dry male voice with an edge]
School gate, half past three
Same boots since eighty-three
Somebody's mother looks me up and down
I nod. I've been around.

[Chorus: synth brass stabs, voices answering]
I'm still in black (still in black)
It was never a phase
Still in black (still in black)
Thirty-five years of the same old ways
You had your fun and you put it back
I'm still in black

[Verse 2: voice warmer, bass bouncing]
Kid runs out with a drawing in her hand
It's me, with a bat, and a marching band
She says, "Dad, you're the only one like this."
I say, "I know." She gives me a kiss.

[Chorus: synth brass stabs, voices answering]
I'm still in black (still in black)
It was never a phase
Still in black (still in black)
Thirty-five years of the same old ways
You had your fun and you put it back
I'm still in black

[Bridge: drums and scratches only, spoken]
Eyeliner's harder with reading glasses.
Worth it.

[Final Chorus: full, with a child's voice on the answers]
I'm still in black (still in black)
It was never a phase
Still in black (still in black)
Thirty-five years of the same old ways
You had your fun and you put it back
I'm still in black

[Outro: bass riff, boots on pavement, a small laugh]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 118 BPM, 4/4, E minor. Bouncy, dark and danceable, a 1984 club track with a grin.

VOICE: Male, dry and slightly nasal with a put-on English edge, half-sung and half-spoken, sure of himself. Voices answer the title line; in the last chorus a child sings the answers. A dry spoken aside in the bridge.

INSTRUMENTS: A bouncing analogue synth bass riff, a drum machine with a big clap and cowbell, synth-brass stabs, record scratches, a string-machine pad, a bright bell-like lead, a tambourine.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, bass, drums and a scratch. 0:16 Verse 1. 0:42 Chorus 1. 1:10 Verse 2. 1:36 Chorus 2. 2:04 Bridge, spoken. 2:18 Final chorus, with the child. 2:48 Outro, bass, boots and a laugh, ends 3:26.

PRODUCTION & MIX: 1984 dark synth-pop: punchy drum machine, fat analogue bass, bright stabs, a dry voice with a short slap echo.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'Eyeliner's harder with reading glasses. Worth it.' at 2:08.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original is a young man asking why people stare. This is the same man at fifty-two, still dressed that way, and the only verdict that matters comes from his daughter.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Stared at, unbothered, loved, proud.
